focus: Angle 7: Skill and command linkage. Compare source-level user intent/choreography with bridge identity, owner mode and model-visible routing.
noveltyJustification: Four findings add command-to-skill ownership and choreography detail; one extends the identity divergence observed in earlier iterations, yielding (4 + 0.5*1) / 5 = 0.90.
keyQuestions: Which one canonical inventory reconciles command metadata, active bridge allow-list rows and doctor routing declarations for all 45 slash commands?
How should command intent and skill intent combine so plain planning and research prompts reach the matching workflow with acceptable recall and precision?
What should a command recommendation show, and which commands can the model invoke directly versus asking first?
How does a plain chat request reach the appropriate command workflow across supported runtimes, and how should skills link to command front doors?
What benchmark evidence, prior art and failure controls should validate the design?
ruledOut: Linking a command only to its parent skill without preserving owner mode and leaf workflow; shared hubs contain distinct routes.
Treating the generated bridge record alone as the full execution recipe; source metadata includes choreography and arguments not shown in the brief.

label: Command metadata already defines userIntent job/signals, ownerMode, argumentHint, and an ordered choreography of parent skill, leaf skill and presentation resource; this is a stronger plain-chat-to-workflow link than a skillId alone.

/deep:research and /deep:review share the system-deep-loop parent but have different owned signals, ownerMode, leaf skill and resource; the model must retain command mode to select the correct workflow beneath a shared skill.

The derived bridge keeps command, skillId, ownerMode, source and runtime scoring fields, while source metadata contains userIntent and choreography; the current rendered brief names a label and scores but not the workflow sequence, so route resolution must carry the metadata resource or load instructions.

Bridge ownership comes from three authored source families: command-metadata files, allow-list rows, and doctor skill_agent tags; all can supply skillId/ownerMode but no one source currently owns the whole 45-file catalog.

The deep-research generated bridge names parent skill system-deep-loop and ownerMode research, but its Python runtime row uses id command-spec-kit-deep-research and owningSkill deep-research; this supports separate canonical command id, parent skill and leaf workflow fields, while contradicting a singular undifferentiated owner key.
